sections.h2: How fast has Clermont grown, and what does that mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Clermont in Lake County counted 28,742 people in the 2010 Census, 43,021 in 2020, and 52,812 in the July 2025 estimate, a gain of 22.8% from the 2020 base. Growth that steep means newer subdivisions, and the Census puts the share of residents under 18 at 22.0%, so many sellers here are families trading up or relocating for work.

A seller with a recent build faces a different set of questions from one with an older house. Roof, plumbing and permit records are fresher on newer homes, while a house with unpermitted work needs sorting out before closing.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Clermont homes?
sections.html:
Median value of an owner-occupied Clermont home is $418,400 for 2020 to 2024, and 68.1% of housing is owner-occupied.

  • Households: 17,609, averaging 2.64 people.
  • Median owner costs with a mortgage: $2,120; without one: $655.
  • Median gross rent: $1,828 a month.
  • Median household income: $82,306.
  • Mean commute: 31.3 minutes.

At 31.3 minutes, the average commute gives buyers a reason to ask about roads and drive times during a showing.

sections.h2: Is my Clermont mailing address inside the city limits?
sections.html:
Not always. The City of Clermont warns that a Clermont address does not guarantee you are inside the city, and it tells owners to look up the parcel on the Lake County Property Appraiser site and read the millage group. A number there means unincorporated Lake County, and letters such as GR or MI point to Groveland or Minneola.

This matters before you sell, because the answer decides which building department issued your permits, which codes applied and which tax bill you will prorate. Check it first, then gather permits from the right office.

sections.h2: What permit questions come up when selling a Clermont house?
sections.html:
The city's Building Services FAQ says almost everything may need a permit, with exceptions such as replacing kitchen cabinets, flooring and painting. Homeowners can pull their own permit only if they own and occupy the residence, and they sign an owner-builder affidavit. The city also warns that a contractor who asks you to pull the permit yourself may be a red flag.

Buyers and their inspectors compare visible work to the record. Items the FAQ names:

  • Fences need a permit, including repair and replacement; height cannot exceed 6 feet behind the building line or 4 feet in front of it.
  • Tree removal needs a permit costing $25 regardless of how many trees, with a site plan of canopy, understory and palm trees.
  • A permit stays active only with one approved inspection every six months.

If you hold a stalled permit, ask Building Services how to close it before listing.

sections.h2: Who owns which pipe at a Clermont house?
sections.html:
The city draws a firm line. Your responsibility for water begins at the point where the line meets the city-owned water meter, and for sewer it begins where your lateral connects to the city main in the street. A leak or blockage on your side is your cost, and one on the city's side is the city's.

The FAQ also says homes with water pressure of 80 psi or more need a pressure-reducing valve under building codes, and the homeowner owns and maintains it. A failing valve or lateral shows up in inspections, so check yours before you list.

sections.h2: What do Clermont's emergency services look like for insurance and buyers?
sections.html:
The Clermont Fire Department runs four stations, at 439 W Highway 50, 2200 Hartwood Marsh Road, 2155 Legends Way and 13341 Hartle Road. The city says its units average a response time under four minutes, and Lake-Sumter EMS provides the ambulance transport.

Buyers like to hear that. It is one more detail for a listing description, and you can cite the city's own page rather than guess.

sections.h2: How does Florida tax a Clermont sale?
sections.html:
Lake County follows the standard rate: 70 cents per $100 of consideration on the deed, with every party to the document liable. The clerk collects it at recording. Your closing agent will show the amount on the settlement statement, so ask for it before agreeing to a price.

The property appraiser sets value each January 1, exemptions must be filed by March 1, and November bills carry a 4 percent discount if paid that month. Because a sale resets a homestead to just value the next January 1, a Clermont buyer's first bill can look higher than yours did, a point worth telling buyers who compare tax records.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Clermont rental house with a tenant inside?
sections.html:
Yes, and the lease usually decides what happens next. A month-to-month tenancy in Florida ends with at least 30 days of notice before the end of a monthly period, a year-to-year tenancy takes 60 days, and a week-to-week tenancy takes 7 days. A tenant late on rent gets a 3-day written notice that leaves out weekends and court holidays.

A landlord who plans to sell with a tenant in place should check the lease for an end date, deposit terms and any right of entry for showings. Cash buyers often take a rented house as it stands, which keeps the tenant's rent coming without a gap.

sections.h2: What if a Clermont owner has fallen behind on the mortgage?
sections.html:
Florida lenders have to go through court. When a judge enters a final judgment, the clerk sets a public sale between 20 and 35 days later, and the high bidder puts down 5 percent. Surplus funds, if any, go to those who file a claim with the clerk before the funds are reported as unclaimed.

Homeowners with a granted homestead exemption on the latest tax roll are presumed to live there, which affects the faster order-to-show-cause route a lender may request. Selling before the sale date pays the loan from proceeds and may leave you some equity. Contact a Florida attorney or the servicer to ask about timing.

sections.h2: How does probate affect selling an inherited Clermont home?
sections.html:
The heirs cannot sell until someone has legal authority, usually a personal representative appointed by the court. Summary administration can apply when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or when the owner died more than two years ago. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is on the state's list of deeds that owe no documentary stamp tax.

Claims against the estate are barred after the later of three months from the first published notice or 30 days from service on a known creditor. Florida does not collect an estate tax for deaths after 2004. Set a date with the probate clerk and a title company before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Clermont house sell for cash?
faqs.a: Often in a few weeks, since a cash buyer skips loan underwriting and the appraisal. Timing still depends on title work and any liens. Ask for a written offer and the closing date in the contract.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit history to sell in Clermont?
faqs.a: A permit history is not required to list, but open permits can delay closing. Call Clermont Building Services to learn whether any permit at your address is unfinished and what inspections are needed.

faqs.q: What if my Clermont house has an old roof or unpermitted work?
faqs.a: You can sell as-is, and cash buyers accept it. Disclose what you know, and expect a buyer to price in the repair or permit cleanup.

faqs.q: Does the seller pay Lake County doc stamps?
faqs.a: Contracts usually assign the deed tax to the seller, but the state makes all parties liable. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, so confirm who pays in writing.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It ends with the sale. The buyer must apply by March 1 for their own exemption, and the property resets to just value the next January 1 after the change of ownership.
